Anna (SRE): Quick follow-up from the customer postmortem — the VPC peering handshake failures we saw with the private deployment look like a recurring pattern (asymmetric routing + MTU mismatch). We need clear ownership, a short timeline, and a lightweight runbook for oncall. Action items below, please ack and add ETAs.

Devon (Eng-Infra): I can own the peering validation/runbook. Will draft steps and a quickchecker script. Target: EOD Thursday.

Rajeev (Private Deploy): I'll own the on-prem adapter change and compatibility checks (NAT/fragmentation handling). Need Sarah to pull customer NAT logs and confirm MTU. Target: next sprint (but can ship a hotfix if logs show consistent failures).

Sarah (Customer Success): Acknowledged. I'll request the NAT logs and network device configs from the customer today and push the ticket for elevated access. Also will schedule a 30m call with their infra team if needed.

Anna (SRE): Proposed minimal runbook items:
- quick triage checklist for oncall
- 3 validation commands to run remotely
- rollback/fallback policy to move customer to dedicated fallback model if peering unstable

Devon (Eng-Infra): Draft runbook (WIP):
```bash
# peering quick checks
ping -c 3 10.0.0.1   # peer control plane
traceroute -m 30 10.0.0.1
# verify AWS peering state
aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=requester-vpc-info.vpc-id,Values=vpc-abc123
```
I'll include an MTU test and a one-line curl against the health endpoint that validates 2-way routing.

Rajeev (Private Deploy): For the on-prem adapter I'll add a conservative fragmentation handler and a retry backoff for the handshake path. Patch will be small but needs a canary in staging with mirrored traffic.

Sarah (Customer Success): ops-bot created INC-4821 for evidence collection. Customer has agreed to provide logs by EOD tomorrow. I'll upload to the ticket.

ops-bot: Ticket INC-4821 created and assigned to: Sarah, Rajeev, Devon. Priority: P2.

Devon (Eng-Infra): Quick question: do we want this runbook in the newplaybooks repo or the private-deploy runbooks repo? I propose private-deploy runbooks so customer-facing oncall can access.

Anna (SRE): private-deploy runbooks repo sounds right. Also add a short checklist for escalation to Dedicated capacity fallback and who approves it (ops@redwood).

Rajeev (Private Deploy): Note: on-prem devices sometimes drop SYN+ACK when MSS is over path MTU. If the customer's network shows PMTU blackholes we should add MSS clamping as an interim fix.

Sarah (Customer Success): I'll ask the customer about evidence of fragmented packets and if they can run a `tcpdump -s 0 -w capture.pcap host 10.0.0.1` during the next window.

Devon (Eng-Infra): I've started a draft PR for the runbook: https://git.redwood.internal/private-deploy/runbooks/pull/27 — comments welcome.

Anna (SRE): Great progress. Final items:
- Devon: runbook PR + quickchecker script (ETA Thu EOD)
- Rajeev: patch for fragmentation/MSS clamping + staging canary (ETA next sprint / expedite if logs confirm)
- Sarah: customer logs & call, update INC-4821 (ETA tomorrow EOD)
- Anna: add escalation policy and fallback procedure to the runbook (I'll do this by Fri)

Please react with :thumbsup: when you ack ownership. If anything blocks you, post here.

Devon (Eng-Infra): :thumbsup:

Rajeev (Private Deploy): :thumbsup:

Sarah (Customer Success): :thumbsup:

Anna (SRE): Thanks — keeping this thread as the single source for the remediation timeline. Will move to a recurring weekly 15m sync if INC-4821 remains open after next week to track patterns.

(END)
